h1: Shrimping Drill: The Foundation of BJJ Movement
seo_title: Shrimping Drill: Solo Mat Movement for BJJ | BJJ Wiki
og_title: Shrimping Drill: Solo Mat Movement for BJJ
description: Master the shrimping drill — the most fundamental BJJ movement. Solo and partner variations, common mistakes, and progressions.
intro_paragraphs: Shrimping (hip escape) is the most fundamental BJJ movement.
Master shrimping in your first month and every other technique becomes easier.

items.text: Builds the lateral hip movement central to guard retention.
Direct application: escaping mount and side control.
Coordinates upper-body frames with lower-body movement.
Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Place both hands on imaginary opponent's hips at chest level.
Drive feet into the mat, lift hips.
Slide hips toward your right shoulder, away from imaginary opponent.
Land on your right side, reset frames, repeat opposite direction.
Practice along the length of mat. 10 reps each direction. Daily.
Partner applies pressure on chest while you shrimp. Practice from mount and side control.
Basic shrimp along the mat, no resistance. Focus on form.
Shrimp from side control with partner applying weight.
Shrimp during full sparring, recovering guard against active attacker.
Pushing with strength alone. Always frame first.
Sliding without lifting creates friction and slow movement.

faq.question: How many reps of shrimping should I do?
faq.answer: 20-30 reps per side daily. Quality over quantity — perfect form beats high volume.

faq.question: Why am I not getting better at guard recovery despite shrimping?
faq.answer: You may be drilling without intent. Visualize the opponent and react to imaginary pressure.
